title: Impact snapshot - Safe-mode enrollment guide (customer-facing draft)
content:
TL;DR
We observed a regional inference disruption affecting a subset of hosted API requests (eu-west-1) between 2027-04-07T22:04 UTC and 2027-04-08T03:12 UTC. Symptoms: elevated 5xx rate for generation endpoints, truncated streaming chunks, and occasional partial KV-cache evictions leading to stale continuations. Root cause (short): a kernel selection regression combined with an aggressive KV-eviction policy under a rare memory pressure pattern.

Who this note is for
- Primary: Customer Success leads who will notify impacted tenants and own enrollment options.
- Secondary: Platform and SRE for operator actions; Solutions Eng for sensitive customers.

Impact summary (customer-facing)
- Affected tenants: ~2.1% of active keys routed to eu-west-1 during the window. Most customers experienced transient errors (rate-limited 5xx) or slower streaming. A smaller cohort (~0.3%) saw truncated/hung streams requiring client-side retry.
- User-visible: higher error rates, a handful of incomplete responses, increased latency for streaming. No evidence of data loss or content corruption.

Safe-mode (what it is)
- A temporary customer-controlled mode that routes requests to a conservative model variant and disables aggressive cache eviction + continuous batching heuristics. Purpose: trade a modest cost/latency increase for stability and deterministic responses.
- Why offer to customers: gives teams immediate self-serve option to reduce exposure while we finish rollout/remediation. Particularly useful for enterprise tenants with strict availability requirements.

Suggested customer-facing statuspage update (short)
- Title: "Partial regional degradation in eu-west-1 — self-serve safe-mode available"
- Body: "We experienced elevated errors for generation APIs in eu-west-1 between 22:04 UTC and 03:12 UTC. Engineers have implemented a conservative safe-mode route available to affected customers while we complete a full fix. Safe-mode reduces likelihood of truncated responses at the cost of slightly higher latency. No customer data was lost. Follow the guide linked here for enrollment steps and verification."

Safe-mode enrollment (customer-facing steps)
1) Console (recommended)
   - Console > Workloads > [Tenant] > Routing Controls > Toggle: "Enable Safe-mode (conservative model & cache)"
   - Expectation: changes are applied in 15–45s. Monitor request success rate on the console dashboard.
2) API (programmatic)
   - POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing
   - Body: {"safe_mode": "on", "mode_profile": "conservative-v1"}
   - Example cURL: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"safe_mode":"on","mode_profile":"conservative-v1"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/tn_12345/routing
   - Expected response: 200 with routing_state = "safe_mode_applied". If you receive 409, retry after 5s — operator rollout is in flight.

How customers can verify it's working
- Succeed rate: 5xx rate should fall to baseline within ~30s of toggle.
- Streaming verification: request a 2k-token streaming generation; confirm no chunk truncation and final delta-id present in last chunk.
- If you have tracing enabled, trace tags: routing.profile=conservative-v1 and kernel.selection=default-safe.

Operator plan (internal notes)
- Priority: finish kernel selection hotfix (PR 2876) and push canary to eu-west-1 tomorrow morning.
- Backstop: ensure KV-eviction thresholds are raised by 15% while canary is validated.
- Communication: send final remediation confirmation when fix is live + verification logs.

Evidence bundle for customers (what we can share)
- Time-bounded query extracts: list of request ids and timestamps (CSV) for affected interval.
- Verification scripts: small curl + trace analyzer to confirm conservative routing tags.
- FAQ snippet for internal CS use: common client questions and recommended replies.

Postmortem summary (customer-facing, short)
- What happened: a change to kernel selection heuristics produced a path that under certain sequence-length/attention patterns consumed more GPU memory than expected; combined with an aggressive new KV-eviction heuristic this led to transient evictions and degraded responses.
- Why it impacted customers: requests in eu-west-1 matched the specific sequence-length distribution more often than in other regions during our traffic spike.
- Mitigation: rolled back kernel rule, increased KV thresholds, and introduced safe-mode route for customers.
- Prevent recurrence: safety gate on kernel heuristic rollouts, telemetry alert for cache-eviction spikes, staged canary expansion policy.

Customer communication templates (short/email)
- Subject: "Action available: temporary safe-mode to reduce truncated responses (eu-west-1)"
- Body (short): "Hi — we recently observed a regional inference disruption that may have affected some of your requests. You can opt into our temporary safe-mode which routes traffic to a conservative model variant to avoid truncated responses. No customer data was lost. Follow this link to enable: <console link>. Reply to this thread or open a priority support ticket if you want us to enable it for you. — Daniel, Customer Success"

Operator checklist for enabling safe-mode on behalf of a customer
- Confirm tenant_id and SLA tier.
- Run: POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/routing with safe_mode:on.
- Validate 3 sample requests succeed end-to-end.
- Attach evidence to ticket: request ids, traces, and console screenshot.

Timeline (ops-focused)
- 2027-04-07T22:04 UTC — error spike detected by automated monitor (5xx > 0.8%).
- 2027-04-07T22:07 UTC — SRE alerted; initial mitigations and increased logging.
- 2027-04-07T22:55 UTC — partial rollback of recent kernel heuristic flagged.
- 2027-04-08T00:30 UTC — KV thresholds adjusted; error rate stabilized.
- 2027-04-08T03:12 UTC — automated monitors returned to nominal.

Unresolved / open questions (notes to self)
- Need to confirm exact list of tenant ids impacted (follow up with infra query). JIRA INC-4821 has partial extract; append full CSV.
- Should we auto-enroll enterprise tenants who opt-in once and then backfill? privacy/consent check.
- Customer-facing metrics: decide if we show pre/post latency P99 in status update (privacy/verbosity tradeoff).

Next steps (internal)
- CS: send targeted email to tenants with >1% error exposure, offer assisted enrollment. (Owner: Leah)
- SRE: finalize kernel hotfix and schedule controlled canary (Owner: Omar).
- Solutions Eng: prepare dedicated verification session for top-10 affected customers (Owner: Priya).

Appendix: short troubleshooting snippets for customers
- If toggle returns 409: wait 10s and retry; if persists, open support with trace id from response.
- If streaming still truncates: collect SDK logs (X-Request-Id) and upload via support portal.

Quick links
- Internal postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/INC-4821-postmortem-draft
- Support playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Customer+Safe+Mode+Playbook
- Operator API ref: https://api.redwood.ai/docs/#routing-control

Notes to self
- Keep draft concise on status page — customers prefer short actionable text + link to deeper doc.
- Confirm wording with legal for phrases around "no data loss".

End of draft.
